title: Manchester United’s Matthijs de Ligt out until next season after surgery on back injury
content:
Manchester United defender Matthijs de Ligt has undergone surgery on a back injury which is set to sideline him until next season.

The 26-year-old has made 14 appearances for United this season but has not played since a 2-1 victory over Crystal Palace in November.

De Ligt’s surgery will also rule him out of playing for the Netherlands in their 2026 World Cup campaign. His last international appearance for Ronald Koeman’s side came in a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania on November 17.

Ruben Amorim, United’s former manager, said at the time that De Ligt’s issue was minor and he was expected to be available again quickly.

The Netherlands international’s recovery has been complicated, however, and he is yet to appear under Michael Carrick, Amorim’s successor as head coach.

In a statement released on Friday, United said that De Ligt has successfully undergone surgery on the issue and that he is expected to return “in the early stages of the 2026-27 season”.

“Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football,” De Ligt said.

“I am grateful to everyone who has supported me throughout a difficult period in my career. I remain as determined as ever to represent Manchester United and play in front of our incredible supporters as soon as possible.”

The former Juventus and Bayern Munich defender returned to training on the grass at United’s Carrington base last month under supervision of the club’s medical staff.

Carrick had previously said that he was “hoping there is a chance” De Ligt may be able to play again this season “without putting any pressure on it”, but he will now play no part in United’s final two Premier League games.

De Ligt had played every minute of United’s top-flight campaign before being sidelined by injury and was named the club’s player of the month for November.

United host Nottingham Forest at Old Trafford on Sunday in their final home game of the Premier League season, before travelling to play Brighton and Hove Albion on 24 May.
